chunks: And by his chain, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleiman ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about the man who marries the slave girl of his wife, then asks her to make him permissible (with her), but she refuses. So he says, 'Then I will divorce you,' and he avoids her bed, so she makes him permissible. He said: 'This is a usurper; so where is he from kindness?'

key_terms.غَاصِبٌ: usurper / one who takes by force

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a husband forcing his wife to permit him to use her slave girl by threatening divorce?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques a husband who coerces his wife into permitting their shared slave girl for his sexual use by threatening divorce and withholding intimacy. The Imam labels him a 'usurper' (*ghasib*) because he leverages marital authority to force consent rather than seeking it through genuine kindness (*lutf*), highlighting the Shia emphasis on mutual respect and voluntary agreement in family dynamics.

en.hubeali: And by his chain, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Suleyman Bin Salih,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the man who marries a slave girl of his wife. Then he asks her if she (the wife) would make him to be in permissibility (with the slave girl), but she refuses. So he is saying, ‘Then I shall divorce you’, and he keeps aside from her bed. So she makes permissibility for him. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a usurper. So where is he from the kindness?’
